text: We want young New Zealanders to be able to join KiwiSaver and stay in it for their working lives.
explanation: A policy preference that young people join and remain in KiwiSaver; a programmatic savings-policy statement without ethical framing.

text: • It has been four years since the Maori Commercial Settlement Act was passed, and most iwi are yet to receive any form of settlement from the Crown.
explanation: States the factual delay in settlements under the Maori Commercial Settlement Act. While it implies a grievance, it contains no explicitly moralized or evaluative terminology (e.g., 'injustice,' 'owed,' 'betrayed'), so per the negative clarification it is coded 0.

text: Those policies have placed the federal government in the driver’s seat,
explanation: A metaphorical description of federal government dominance ('driver's seat'); political description without ethical content.

text: This has resulted in increased pressure in the health system and failed outcomes for healthcare staff, patients and the public.
explanation: Describes system pressure and 'failed outcomes' for staff and patients — a performance critique, not an appeal to ethical standards, rights, or desert.

text: •  More than two in every three New  Zealanders  does unpaid work outside their  own households.
explanation: A bare statistic about the prevalence of unpaid work; purely descriptive.

text: ACARA will work with States and Territories to ensure the Cadetships contribute towards state based senior awards, in the same way as other approved subjects under the National Curriculum
explanation: Administrative detail about ACARA coordinating cadetship recognition within curricula; procedural and technical.

text: That’s why President Obama and Democrats in Congress have enacted infrastructure investments that will
explanation: A claim about infrastructure investments enacted by Democrats; programmatic/economic content only.

text: Increased funding for early childhood education by $550 million, or 40 per cent, since 2008.
explanation: A fiscal spending figure on early childhood education, matching the negative clarification's exclusion of spending descriptions.

text: Labor’s Infrastructure Australia is a secretive organisation.
explanation: Calling Infrastructure Australia a 'secretive organisation' is an evaluative process critique, but it does not invoke an ethical concept (such as corruption or dishonesty) or a moral duty; it remains a thin administrative/political attack rather than moral rhetoric. Borderline, but I judged it to lack the explicit ethical framework the codebook requires.

text: South Island domestic and industrial users will have their price discounted.
explanation: A pricing commitment for South Island energy users; purely technical/economic.

text: Labor has done little to educate the public on the benefits of cleaner fuels.
explanation: A criticism of Labor's inaction on public education about cleaner fuels; a performance critique without moral terminology.

text: In 1997, a single person on the average industrial wage paid 22% of their income in income tax.
explanation: A bare statistic about income tax paid in 1997; purely descriptive.

text: Together we're the co-leaders of the Green party
explanation: A self-descriptive statement about party co-leadership; no normative content.

text: without allowing emissions from aviation to undermine our goal of a zero-carbon Britain by 2050.
explanation: Frames aviation emissions policy around the technical goal of a zero-carbon Britain by 2050; environmental target-setting without explicitly moralized language.

text: The development of an ‘alternative growth pole’ along the Atlantic Corridor will be pursued.
explanation: A regional development commitment ('alternative growth pole' along the Atlantic Corridor); economic/spatial planning, no ethical content.

text: This will be underpinned by new rights for patients.
explanation: The reference to 'new rights for patients' invokes rights-based entitlement language — an appeal to what patients are owed — rather than a purely technical description. I note ambiguity since patient rights are statutory/consumer-style rights rather than fundamental human rights, but the explicit 'rights' framing is normative.

text: Current investment in developing and protecting the Australian farm sector does not recognise the large contribution farmers make to our economy.
explanation: Argues that investment fails to recognise farmers' economic contribution; this is a contribution-based economic argument using economic terminology, lacking explicitly moralized desert or fairness language, so it falls under the negative clarification.

text: We recognize that adoption costs can be high and in some cases prohibitive for families.
explanation: A sympathetic but descriptive observation that adoption costs can be prohibitive for families; it identifies a barrier without deploying ethical concepts, duty, or desert language.

text: We will increase access to the arts for young people, particularly those of disadvantaged backgrounds,
explanation: A programmatic pledge to increase arts access for young people, including those from 'disadvantaged backgrounds.' While equity-oriented in aim, it lacks explicitly moralized or evaluative terminology (unlike 'access for all, regardless of...'), so under the negative clarification it is excluded as a beneficial social policy stated in neutral terms.

text: Direct this new spending to health, education, and a few carefully targeted initiatives.
explanation: Purely programmatic spending directive toward health and education with no evaluative or normative moral terminology, matching the negative clarification about fiscal spending and generic policy commitments.

text: The Green Party is committed to bringing rail services into public ownership and control.
explanation: A policy commitment to public ownership of rail services; it lacks any explicit moralized, evaluative language or appeal to ethical frameworks.

text: provide direct and meaningful support to land managers in delivering ecoservices; | and
explanation: Administrative support for land managers delivering ecoservices; technical policy language without ethical concepts, duty, or desert claims.

text: and providing other services as required, thus contributing to Ireland’s political and economic well being.
explanation: Descriptive statement about services contributing to political and economic well-being; utilitarian framing with no moral terminology.

text: • Conflicting roles and responsibilities.
explanation: A bullet point noting conflicting roles and responsibilities; purely descriptive administrative content.

text: An SNP government will strive to ensure that Scotland becomes a world leader in securing a sustainable environment
explanation: An aspirational commitment to environmental leadership. Per the negative clarification, environmental goals without explicitly moralized language are coded 0.

text: With the investment that we are promising in hospital buildings,
explanation: References promised investment in hospital buildings; infrastructure spending with no moral or evaluative framing.

text: The question that should still be asked of Labor is:
explanation: A rhetorical setup for a question to Labor; contains no ethical concepts or normative claims.

text: And with new laws to crack down on domestic violence,
explanation: A programmatic statement about new laws addressing domestic violence. While the underlying issue is serious, the sentence itself is a law-and-order policy commitment without explicit moralized or evaluative terminology (e.g., justice, rights, intolerability).

text: Fine Gael will support the on-going nationwide roll out of the “Food Dudes” Fruit and Vegetable Promotion programme to all primary schools in Ireland.
explanation: Commitment to roll out a fruit and vegetable promotion programme in schools; purely programmatic education/health policy.

text: Every board shall publish before March of each year an annual report on  its own activities as opposed to the wider work of the state body.
explanation: Administrative requirement for boards to publish annual reports; procedural language with no moral content.

text: In particular, as we expand access to talking therapies we expect many more people to recover and be able to seek work again.
explanation: Health policy expectation about recovery and return to work via talking therapies; utilitarian framing without moral terminology.

text: and free up  resources  for whānau development.
explanation: Administrative reallocation of resources for whānau development; no explicit ethical or normative language.

text: We will give 1 weeks paid Parental leave for either parent to take, giving them more choice.
explanation: A paid parental leave policy offer framed around parental choice; programmatic benefit with no appeal to fairness, rights, or desert.

text: Policy alignment will ensure the wise use of public dollars.
explanation: 'Wise use of public dollars' refers to efficient fiscal management, not an ethical standard; administrative/economic framing.

text: At £1.4 Trillion, that equates to £54,353 per household;
explanation: A fiscal statistic equating debt to a per-household figure; purely economic, matching the negative example on fiscal critique.

text: maintain the Defence Forces’ proud reputation in peacekeeping
explanation: Maintaining the Defence Forces' 'proud reputation' in peacekeeping is descriptive of reputation rather than an explicit invocation of virtue or duty; closest to a generic commitment. Borderline, but 'proud' here modifies reputation rather than deploying a moral argument.

text: The Nationals are determined to eliminate the divide between those living in and those living outside major capital cities, including any limitation on access to a fair legal system that respects the rights and responsibilities of all Australians.
explanation: Explicitly invokes ethical concepts listed in the codebook: a 'fair legal system' that 'respects the rights and responsibilities of all Australians' — fairness, respect, and rights are key markers of moral rhetoric.

text: These moves will eliminate remaining inequality in the income tax system and enhance its progressive nature.
explanation: The pledge to 'eliminate remaining inequality' invokes equality, an ethical concept explicitly listed in the codebook's clarification as a marker of moral rhetoric.

text: It is now enshrined in law that we must pay 0.7 per cent of our Gross National Income (GNI) on aid every year.
explanation: Describes a legal requirement ('enshrined in law') to spend 0.7% of GNI on aid; the obligation referenced is statutory, not framed in moral or ethical terms.

text: Caroline Lucas and housing In July 2014 Caroline Lucas MP introduced a Housing (Affordability, Supply and Tenant Protection) Bill to highlight the problems faced by private tenants.
explanation: A descriptive account of an MP introducing a housing bill; factual reporting of legislative activity without moralized language.

text: Support for 2,500 additional aged care beds;
explanation: Support for additional aged care beds; a programmatic spending commitment with no ethical framing.

text: Develop new community policing structures, through local policing forums in individual communities, to reconnect the Gardaí and local communities in a spirit of genuine partnership.
explanation: Proposes community policing structures in a 'spirit of genuine partnership'; this is programmatic language about institutional design, not moral terminology.

text: We will: save you money by cutting government waste
explanation: Saving money by cutting government waste; purely fiscal/administrative framing.

text: Ireland should be the best place in the world to grow up, and to grow old.
explanation: An aspirational statement that Ireland should be the 'best place' to grow up and grow old; a generic political aspiration lacking explicit moralized or evaluative ethical terminology, per the negative clarification.

text: Ministerial Cars: We will end the automatic entitlement to a State car for every Government Minister.
explanation: Ending automatic entitlement to ministerial state cars; an administrative/perk reform. 'Entitlement' here describes a benefit, not a moral desert claim.

text: If you can’t trust Labour and National to go public about poisoned baby milk then what on earth can you trust them on.
explanation: The rhetorical question 'what on earth can you trust them on' impugns the honesty and trustworthiness of opponents — a judgment of personal/civic virtue (integrity). The accusation that parties failed to disclose poisoned baby milk frames a moral failing, going beyond technical or administrative critique.

text: All TDs will be entitled to put forward proposals for legislation and a lottery at the start of each session will determine which Bills will be debated.
explanation: A procedural reform for TDs to submit bills selected by lottery; institutional mechanics without moral language.

text: We will put in train preparations for the 100th anniversary of the Easter Rising, in a manner that honours the contribution of the men and women of Easter Week,
explanation: The commitment to commemorate the Easter Rising 'in a manner that honours the contribution of the men and women of Easter Week' invokes honour and patriotic virtue — ideals of human virtue listed in the codebook (e.g., patriotism, respect).

text: We will support sensible immigration policies that meet our economic needs
explanation: Support for 'sensible' immigration policies meeting 'economic needs'; explicitly utilitarian/economic framing without ethical concepts.

text: Establishing the right accountability framework for schools.
explanation: Establishing the 'right' accountability framework for schools; 'right' here means appropriate/correct in an administrative sense, not a moral right.

text: Republicans share President Bush's understanding that just as events in Europe determined the outcome of the Cold War, events in the broader Middle East will set the course for the victory of free nations in the War on Terror.
explanation: A geopolitical claim that Middle East events will determine the 'victory of free nations in the War on Terror.' Although 'free nations' carries some normative connotation, the sentence is framed as a predictive/strategic assessment rather than an explicit appeal to ethical standards or moral duty. Ambiguous, but coded 0 for lack of explicit moral terminology.

text: • there is appropriate time for debate to be conducted.
explanation: Procedural point about appropriate debate time; administrative content.

text: All recreational fishers should help police the system to ensure that there is no room for poachers and quasi ‘recreational’ fishers who sell or raffle their catches.
explanation: Calls on recreational fishers to help police the system against poachers; this is regulatory enforcement language concerning illegal fishing. 'Poachers' is a legal/regulatory category rather than explicit moral condemnation, so it falls under administrative enforcement.

text: •  Created  2000 jobs  during the recession  through state housing upgrades.
explanation: Claims credit for creating jobs through state housing upgrades; descriptive economic achievement.

text: Constitutional stability for Northern Ireland;
explanation: 'Constitutional stability for Northern Ireland' is a descriptive political goal without moral terminology.

text: It will dismantle the dysfunctional Health Service Executive (HSE) that was created by Micheál Martin in 2004,
explanation: Dismantling the 'dysfunctional' HSE; 'dysfunctional' is an administrative performance evaluation, not an ethical judgment.

text: conflicts with long-term strategies to cut waste volumes by recycling and reduction, requires huge scale to operate efficiently and generates large volumes of traffic.
explanation: Technical critique of waste strategy (scale, efficiency, traffic); no moral language.

text: and transition to a prosperous, decarbonized economy.
explanation: Transition to a prosperous, decarbonized economy; economic/environmental framing without ethical concepts.

text: This will support our aim to make Britain the best place in Europe, and one of the top five worldwide, to do business by 2020.
explanation: Aim to make Britain a top place to do business; economic competitiveness framing.

text: The Nationals believe that, when wealth is generated in a region, a fair share of the resulting government revenue should be returned to that region and to regional Australia more generally.
explanation: The claim that a 'fair share' of government revenue should be returned to regions explicitly deploys the ethical concept of fairness and a normative desert claim ('should be returned'), both key markers in the codebook.

text: Half a million of us regularly play sport, while 400,000 volunteer as coaches, match officials and referees.
explanation: Descriptive statistics on sport participation and volunteering; no evaluative moral language.

text: We recognise the contribution that Mäori enterprise and entrepreneurship has made to our nation's economy.
explanation: Recognising Māori enterprise contributions to the economy; a descriptive acknowledgment without explicit ethical or normative terminology.

text: We will: Work to secure the full implementation of the Military Covenant in Northern Ireland.
explanation: A commitment to implement the Military Covenant; framed as a policy implementation pledge. While a 'covenant' implies obligation, the sentence itself is programmatic and does not explicitly deploy moralized language such as duty, desert, or virtue. Borderline, coded 0.

text: abolish the current 2% limit for funding political parties, which acts against new and smaller parties and could be seen as supporting the status quo;
explanation: Abolishing the 2% party funding limit; describes effects on smaller parties and the status quo in structural terms without explicitly moralized language like 'unfair' or 'unjust.'

text: After so long in office, Mr Howard has forgotten what fairness actually means.
explanation: 'Mr Howard has forgotten what fairness actually means' explicitly invokes the ethical concept of fairness — a key marker listed in the codebook — and applies it as a moral character critique.

text: • develop Parents as First Teacher (PAFT) programmes across the country.
explanation: Developing Parents as First Teacher programmes; programmatic education policy.

text: We will crackdown on overseas producers who don’t cooperate with anti-dumping investigations
explanation: Crackdown on overseas producers not cooperating with anti-dumping investigations; trade enforcement policy without moral framing.

text: Labour will ensure that the Defence  Forces are appropriately equipped and staffed to meet Ireland’s  obligations to United Nations and EU peacekeeping missions.
explanation: Ensuring Defence Forces are equipped to meet obligations to UN/EU peacekeeping missions; the 'obligations' referenced are institutional commitments, framed administratively.

text: Processing of applications and decision-making is subject to long delays, while the absence of legislation means there is frequent resort to the Courts for judicial review.
explanation: Describes administrative delays and resort to judicial review due to absent legislation; a procedural critique without moral terminology.
